Simulating chemical systems is highly sought after and computationally challenging, as the number of degrees
of freedom increases exponentially with the size of the system. Quantum computers have been proposed as
a computational means to overcome this bottleneck , thanks to their capability of representing this amount of
information efficiently. Most efforts so far have been centered around determining the ground states of chemical

methods.value: The proposed framework employs a limited set of attainable atomic initial states and dynamically prepares input states for a reaction of interest through a scattering process, specifically by hierarchically combining atomic states through scattering.

problems.value: Simulating chemical systems is highly sought after and computationally challenging due to the exponential increase in degrees of freedom with system size.

hypotheses.value: A heuristically guided approach based on efficient routines can solve chemical simulation problems requiring quantum circuits of size scaling polynomially in relevant system parameters.

evidence.value: The approach finds good initial states for dynamics simulation by assembling them in a scattering tree, and it discusses a variety of quantities of chemical interest that can be measured after the quantum simulation of a process.

conclusions.value: The paper demonstrates a new approach to quantum chemical simulations that avoids the hardness of ground state problems and enables the simulation of a wide range of chemically relevant phenomena.
